haiku-low.q1: It still signs in to the same account. Users are found by Google sub, not email, and Google never changes users.email.
haiku-low.q2: The user must submit the correct password on the confirm page. Then the user_identities row is inserted, the pending link deleted, and start_session runs.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. The fifth failure locks the account for 15 minutes, resets failed_logins to 0, and deletes the pending link. No link is created.
haiku-low.q4: No matching user: a new user with no password and verified email is created, plus a user_identities row, then a session. Email not verified: refused, pointed to email and password, nothing created.
haiku-low.q5: At 12 minutes the state has expired, so an error page shows and nothing changes. A second load finds the state already deleted, so the same error page shows.
haiku-low.q6: start_session(user_id) runs: any old sid session is deleted, a new session row is inserted, and the sid cookie is set. The old sid session is removed.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required. If the Google sub is linked to another user, the link is refused as already in use and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, for 10 minutes. The callback deletes the state on use, so it is used once; otherwise it expires after 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q9: In Redis for 10 minutes, held as a pending link for one user and one Google account. The browser holds its id in an HttpOnly cookie. Correct password, fifth failure, locked account, or expiry deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In the permanent Postgres user_identities table. Unique constraints on google_sub and user_id enforce one Google account per user and one user per Google account.
haiku-low.q11: The user is sent back to the entry point with a neutral message, and nothing is stored. Whether the exchange is retried is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q12: The state record in Redis stores the entry point (login or settings) and, for settings, the user id. The callback reads these from Redis, so the link goes to the user who started it.

sonnet.q1: They sign in to the same account. Linked users are found by sub, never email, and Google never changes users.email.
sonnet.q2: The user must submit the account's password on the Confirm password page (pending link saved in Redis, 10 min). A correct password inserts the user_identities row, deletes the pending link, and then start_session runs. Not allowed if that user already has a Google link (refused), and a locked account shows the locked message.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins and shows an error on the same page. The fifth failure locks the account for 15 minutes (locked_until set, failed_logins reset to 0), shows 'Account temporarily locked', and deletes the pending link. No link is created.
sonnet.q4: Verified email matching no user: create a user with no password and a verified email, insert a user_identities row, then start_session. email_verified false: refuse, tell the user to use email and password, and create nothing.
sonnet.q5: Error page and nothing changes. The state is expired (10 min) after 12 minutes, or already used and deleted on the second load.
sonnet.q6: The same session as a password login, via start_session(user_id): it inserts a session row in sessions and sets the sid cookie, then redirects to next or /home. Any old sid session is deleted. No new session type.
sonnet.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required. Settings mode only links and does not compare emails. If the sub is already linked to another user, it is refused ('Google account already in use'), and nothing changes. If it is already linked to this user, it says already linked. If this user already has a different Google link, it is refused.
sonnet.q8: In Redis, together with the entry point, user id (settings only) and next value, for 10 minutes. The callback takes and deletes the state in one step on use (so it is single-use), or it expires after 10 minutes.
sonnet.q9: In Redis for 10 minutes as the pending link. The document does not say exactly which fields it holds, though it is for one user and one Google account. The browser refers to it by its id in an HttpOnly cookie. It is deleted by a correct password, the fifth wrong password, an already-locked account, or expiry.
sonnet.q10: In the Postgres table user_identities (permanent). user_id references users(id) with ON DELETE CASCADE. A unique google_sub gives one user per Google account, and a unique user_id gives one Google account per user.
sonnet.q11: The user goes back to the entry point (login or Settings) with a neutral message. Nothing is stored. Retry: NOT STATED beyond going back to the entry point (no automatic retry is described).
sonnet.q12: The entry point (login or settings) and, for settings, the user id are saved in Redis with the state at start. The callback reads them when it takes the state. Settings mode links the identity to that stored user id.
